question.problem:
The probability mass function of the random variables $X$ and $Y$ are given below.
$x$ $1$ $2$ $3$ $4$
$f(x)$ $\frac{1}{6}$ $\frac{1}{3}$ $\frac{1}{6}$ $\frac{1}{3}$
$y$ $1$ $5$ $10$
$f(y)$ $\frac{5}{8}$ $\frac{1}{8}$ $\frac{1}{4}$

Find $\text{E}[4Y-3X].$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that if $X$ and $Y$ are random variables (not necessarily independent), and $a$ and $b$ are constants, then

$$
\text{E}[aX+bY]=a\text{E}[X]+b\text{E}[Y].
$$

First, let's find $\text{E}[X]$ and $\text{E}[Y].$ If $X$ is defined on a sample space ${S}_{x},$ then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\sum }_{x\in {S}_{x}}x\cdot f(x) \\  & =1\cdot \frac{1}{6}+2\cdot \frac{1}{3}+3\cdot \frac{1}{6}+4\cdot \frac{1}{3} \\  & =\frac{8}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, if $Y$ is defined on a sample space ${S}_{y},$ then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & ={\sum }_{y\in {S}_{y}}y\cdot f(y) \\  & =1\cdot \frac{5}{8}+5\cdot \frac{1}{8}+10\cdot \frac{1}{4} \\  & =\frac{15}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[4Y-3X] & =\text{E}[4Y]+\text{E}[-3X] \\  & =4\text{E}[Y]-3\text{E}[X] \\  & =4\cdot \frac{15}{4}-3\cdot \frac{8}{3} \\  & =7.\end{aligned}
$$
